extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quintile of intake
extraction.population: men with incident, histologically confirmed prostate cancer and hospital controls admitted for acute, non-neoplastic conditions

sample_size.excerpt: Cases were 1294 men with incident, histologically confirmed prostate cancer, and admitted to the major teaching and general hospitals of study areas. Controls were 1451 men admitted for acute, non-neoplastic conditions to the same hospital network.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 1294 + 1451 = 2745

cases.excerpt: Cases were 1294 men with incident, histologically confirmed prostate cancer, and admitted to the major teaching and general hospitals of study areas.

effect_size.excerpt: A direct association with prostate cancer was found for starch intake (OR = 1.4 in the highest versus the lowest quintile of intake; 95% CI: 1.1-1.8), whereas an inverse association emerged for polyunsaturated fatty acids (OR = 0.8; 95% CI: 0.6-1.0).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among polyunsaturated fatty acids, linolenic acid (OR = 0.7; 95% CI: 0.6-0.9) and linoleic acid (OR = 0.8; 95% CI: 0.6-1.0) were inversely related to prostate cancer.
